grades.quote: Note that writing `satp` does not imply any ordering constraints between page-table updates and subsequent address translations, nor does it imply any invalidation of address-translation caches. If the new address space’s page tables have been modified, or if an ASID is reused, it may be necessary to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction (see Section 12.2.1) after, or in some cases before, writing `satp` .
grades.reason: Directly connects changing the address-space context through satp with the separate ordering and translation-cache synchronization provided by SFENCE.VMA.

grades.quote: In particular, if a leaf PTE is modified but a subsuming SFENCE.VMA is not executed, either the old translation or the new translation will be used, but the choice is unpredictable. The behavior is otherwise well-defined.
grades.reason: Explains why synchronization is needed to avoid stale translations, but does not explain changing satp.

grades.quote: Executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction guarantees that any previous stores already visible to the current RISC-V hart are ordered before certain implicit references by subsequent instructions in that hart to the memory-management data structures. The specific set of operations ordered by SFENCE.VMA is determined by _rs1_ and _rs2_ , as described below. SFENCE.VMA is also used to invalidate entries in the address-translation cache associated with a hart (see Section 12.3.2).
grades.reason: Directly explains SFENCE.VMA’s ordering and cache-invalidation purposes, but not satp’s page-table-switch effect.

grades.quote: _High-performance implementations will be able to pipeline the address-translation cache invalidation operations, and will defer any pipeline stalls or other memory ordering enforcement until an SFENCE.W.INVAL, SFENCE.INVAL.IR, SFENCE.VMA, HFENCE.GVMA, or HFENCE.VVMA instruction is executed._
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary context about translation-cache invalidation and ordering, but focuses on Svinval alternatives rather than satp switching.
